title: Audit logs & admin activity review with Aurora Payments
summary: Redwood walk-through of audit log schema, what admin activity is captured, export/streaming options (S3, webhook, syslog), default retention (90 days), paid longer-retention options, and encryption/KMS handling. Customer asked about evidence for SOC 2, how RBAC/SSO events are logged, and how to integrate logs with their Splunk stack. Action items: send SOC2 report link, sample log export, and schedule demo of export pipeline.
next_steps: Marcus to send audit-log schema and 48-hr sample export (S3 link)
Lena to share SOC 2 report and compliance pack link
Schedule follow-up demo to show streaming export into customer's Splunk on 2026-03-29 11:00 PT

Lena Ortiz (Redwood) - share SOC 2 report and compliance pack - due 2026-03-24
Carlos Rivera (Aurora) - confirm Splunk ingestion team and syslog endpoint - due 2026-03-26
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-22 10:30am PT | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Aurora Head of Security), Carlos Rivera (Aurora SRE), Emily Tan (Aurora Product)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro i'm Lena, AE at Redwood, and Marcus is our SE. we're here to walk through audit logs and admin activity for Aurora Payments.
[00:23] Marcus Chen: hey all. agenda is: what events we capture, formats, export options (S3/webhook/syslog), retention defaults, and encryption/KMS notes. feel free to interrupt.
[01:12] Priya Singh: thanks. high level for us we need to show auditors that admin actions are captured (role grants, user creation, key rotations) and trace who did what and when. also need retention evidence.
[01:35] Marcus Chen: absolutely. quick caveat i'll call out that some names might be transcribed slightly off in the recording; but the events themselves are standard. we capture 4 broad buckets: admin config changes, auth events, data-access events, and deployment/execution events.
[02:02] Carlos Rivera: when you say data-access events do you include model debug downloads and export of PII?
[02:10] Marcus Chen: yes we log dataset export events, model download/deploy, and explicit export actions. for example: export_dataset, create_api_key, revoke_api_key, role_grant, role_revoke, user_login_success, user_login_failure, sso_assertion, kms_key_use, kms_key_rotate, and admin_console_login.
[02:45] Emily Tan: how are timestamps represented? we need rfc3339 with tz.
[02:50] Marcus Chen: rfc3339 UTC by default, and there's a sequence id to correlate across requests.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: sample schema link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/audit-logs (we'll share after).
[04:05] Priya Singh: auditors also want to know access to admin console UI, who viewed logs, and if we can filter by user.
[04:20] Marcus Chen: yes event includes actor (user id + email), actor_role, ip_address, user_agent, resource_type, resource_id, action, before/after for config changes, and optional request_payload reference. note: request_payloads that contain sensitive PII are redacted by default and only stored as pointers to secure blobs with limited access.
[05:10] Carlos Rivera: retention what is default?
[05:15] Marcus Chen: default retention for audit logs is 90 days on hosted plans. we offer add-ons for 1 year and multi-year retention for enterprise customers via a retained-logs package that stores encrypted logs in customer-dedicated buckets.
[05:40] Priya Singh: is it possible to ship logs to our S3 in our account? we have strict controls and want logs to live in our environment.
[05:55] Lena Ortiz: yes we support cross-account S3 export (push), and also streaming via webhook or syslog for SIEM ingestion. we can also stream to Splunk HEC endpoint.
[06:30] Carlos Rivera: any delivery guarantees? e.g., at-least-once vs best-effort?
[06:36] Marcus Chen: delivery modes: batch export (daily or hourly bundles) and real-time streaming. streaming is best-effort with retry/backoff and dead-letter queue; for critical audits we recommend S3 cross-account or our delivery with guaranteed delivery retries and checksum verification.
[07:10] Priya Singh: encryption at rest and in transit? and KMS integration?
[07:18] Marcus Chen: all logs are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+), and at rest. for hosted customers we manage keys by default, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP CMEK / Azure Key Vault for private/dedicated deployments. when CMK is used, logs stored in our buckets or cross-account buckets can be encrypted with your key. we also log key usage events (kms_key_use, kms_key_rotate).
[08:05] Emily Tan: do you include audit trail for role changes, like who granted admin role and when?
[08:12] Marcus Chen: yes role_grant and role_revoke include before/after role bindings and the admin that performed the change.
[09:00] Priya Singh: how long do you keep the mapping from user id to email? since for retention we might need pseudonymization.
[09:10] Marcus Chen: we can pseudonymize identifiers after a configurable window. by default, identifying fields are kept as-is for 90 days; we can offer policies to hash or redact after X days for compliance.
[10:00] Carlos Rivera: integration with SIEM Splunk specifically. how does ingestion look?
[10:08] Marcus Chen: options: push to your S3 bucket (we deposit ndjson/jsonl bundles hourly), streaming to webhook or syslog, direct Splunk HEC integration, or we can ship via a connector. payloads include a newline-delimited JSON event per line.
[10:45] Priya Singh: is there a schema we can validate against?
[10:50] Marcus Chen: yes we'll provide a JSON Schema and sample payloads.
[12:00] Lena Ortiz: quick Q: auditors ask for evidence of immutability do you provide write-once logs or object versioning?
[12:10] Marcus Chen: we support S3 object lock on delivered exports to customer buckets, and our internal storage has append-only histories with checksums and tamper-evidence metadata. for enterprise packages we can enable immutability windows.
[13:05] Emily Tan: what about RBAC/SSO events do you log successful and failed SSO assertions, and can we map them to sessions?
[13:15] Marcus Chen: yes sso_assertion_success and sso_assertion_failure events contain assertion_id, identity_provider, and session_id. session start/stop events are also present.
[14:00] Carlos Rivera: are API key uses logged with request ids to trace actions?
[14:07] Marcus Chen: all API calls have request_id and api_key_id. we capture request metadata and response status.
[15:00] Priya Singh: auditors will want sampling of logs and a how-to to reproduce a trace.
[15:07] Marcus Chen: we'll provide a 48-hour sample export with synthetic but realistic events and a mapping doc to show how to chase an incident.
[16:20] Lena Ortiz: question about who can access audit logs in Redwood console RBAC controls?
[16:30] Marcus Chen: logs access is governed by roles. we have pre-baked roles (admin, security_reader, developer) and custom roles. admin role can view/download logs; security_reader can view and create exports but not modify retention. all accesses generate audit events too.
[17:05] Priya Singh: do you integrate with our IdP for SSO and SCIM provisioning?
[17:12] Marcus Chen: yes SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning supported; provisioning events are logged too.
[18:00] Carlos Rivera: are there examples of policy-based alerts for suspicious admin activity?
[18:08] Marcus Chen: yes Redwood Console supports alerting rules (e.g., large export, multiple failed logins, new key creation). alerts can post to webhook/Slack/Syslog and can include a link to the raw log.
[19:30] Priya Singh: for compliance pack, do you provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO docs?
[19:36] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll share SOC 2 and ISO attestations and our compliance pack link after the call.
[20:10] Emily Tan: any PII redaction guarantees?
[20:18] Marcus Chen: we redact sensitive fields by default and provide pointers to secure blobs; full payloads can be made available under stricter controls and only via cross-account S3 delivery to your bucket.
[21:00] Priya Singh: what about change history for retention policy changes is that separately tracked?
[21:08] Marcus Chen: yes retention_policy_change events are emitted for admin changes to retention and include before/after values and actor.
[22:15] Carlos Rivera: how do you handle live exports during incident response? can we request immediate dumps?
[22:22] Marcus Chen: yes we have an on-demand export API that can produce a filtered export and push to your S3 or HEC endpoint; for urgent needs we also support authenticated temporary links with short TTL.
[23:45] Priya Singh: sample log is it NDJSON?
[23:50] Marcus Chen: yes ndjson/jsonl. each line an event; we'll include JSON Schema.
[24:30] Emily Tan: about searchability do you provide indices or do we index on our side?
[24:36] Marcus Chen: Redwood Console offers search/filters for 90-day window; for longer retention we recommend shipping to your SIEM for indexing.
[25:40] Lena Ortiz: a couple of customer-specific notes Aurora needs cross-account S3 export and Splunk HEC; they may opt for 1-year retention.
[26:05] Priya Singh: SLAs is log export covered under SLA?
[26:12] Marcus Chen: exports are covered for enterprise customers under the dedicated package; hosted has nominal best-effort but we guarantee delivery retries for retained-logs module. SLA specifics we'll include in the compliance pack.
[28:00] Carlos Rivera: do you store request payloads for debug? you mentioned pointers earlier but can we opt into full payload retention?
[28:10] Marcus Chen: yes under strict controls full payloads containing PII can only be stored if exported to your customer bucket or if you enable secure blob retention with additional controls and access logs.
[30:00] Priya Singh: auditability can you prove chain of custody for log copies?
[30:08] Marcus Chen: we maintain checksums, delivery receipts, and signing metadata for delivered archives; cross-account S3 delivery includes server-side checksums and we can provide delivery receipts as evidence.
[33:00] Lena Ortiz: discussion about legal/regulatory needs data residency?
[33:10] Marcus Chen: logs can be stored in region-specific buckets (US/EU/APAC) depending on your contract and deployment. for private deployments you control the region fully.
[35:00] Carlos Rivera: any gotchas with syslog format?
[35:06] Marcus Chen: syslog maps fields into structured key=value pairs; we recommend HEC or S3 for full fidelity. syslog may truncate very large payloads.
[36:20] Priya Singh: timeline for enabling 1-year retention?
[36:25] Marcus Chen: typically 2-3 weeks for setup with cross-account S3 and IAM configuration, faster if you already have a bucket and Splunk endpoints ready.
[38:00] Emily Tan: pricing ballpark for 1-year retention?
[38:08] Lena Ortiz: we'll share pricing in the follow-up; depends on data volumes and retention tier.
[40:00] Carlos Rivera: are admin console accesses also exportable in logs?
[40:06] Marcus Chen: yes console_view and console_download events show UI activity.
[42:00] Priya Singh: are historical logs queryable through API?
[42:08] Marcus Chen: yes for the retention window; for shipped exports you query your own storage.
[44:00] Emily Tan: how do you handle GDPR/DSR requests tied to logs?
[44:05] Marcus Chen: we support data subject requests logs can be redacted or filtered; for hosted-managed logs we follow legal process with customer approval; for cross-account S3 delivery the data is in your control.
[46:00] Lena Ortiz: ok, we're getting close to time quick recap and next steps.
[46:10] Marcus Chen: recap: we'll send audit-log schema and 48-hr sample export, Lena will send SOC2/ISO docs, we'll schedule export demo into Splunk on 2026-03-29 at 11am PT, and provide 1-year retention pricing.
[46:45] Priya Singh: sounds good. couple clarifying Qs who will be our contact for the Splunk integration?
[46:52] Lena Ortiz: Marcus will lead the integration work.
[47:10] Carlos Rivera: i'll confirm internal syslog/HEC endpoints and share by Friday.
[47:20] Emily Tan: thanks, that works.
[48:00] Priya Singh: anything else on encryption keys? we might require HSM-backed keys.
[48:06] Marcus Chen: we support HSM-backed key stores via customer-managed KMS (AWS/CloudHSM options) for dedicated/private deployments would be part of enterprise contract.
[49:30] Lena Ortiz: action items captured; we'll follow up with links and sample exports.
[50:00] Priya Singh: thanks everyone.
[50:10] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., KV cache spelled as V K cache) and speaker overlaps. References shared: https://redwood.example.com/docs/audit-logs, SOC2 report link (to be shared), sample S3 export will be provided as a pre-signed link.
